interest: U.S. moves in 1940 to keep Japanese naval vessels out of Hawaii.
overview: This file comprises State Department records from October and November 1940 regarding proposed and actual visits by Japanese public vessels, naval auxiliaries, and merchant ships to ports of the United States and the Territory of Hawaii. The central correspondence involves a confidential dossier initiated by Admiral J. O. Richardson (Commander in Chief, U.S. Fleet) and Admiral Claude C. Bloch (Commandant, Fourteenth Naval District, Pearl Harbor), forwarded by the Chief of Naval Operations to the Department of State, and shared with the Treasury and Interior Departments. The communications focus on national security concerns regarding espionage and propaganda by Japanese crews during visits to Hawaiian ports following the August 1940 visit of the naval tanker Shiriya, leading to a policy of denying entry to Japanese public ships and utilizing Treasury customs authority under the June 27, 1940 Presidential Proclamation to control foreign crews. Associated cross-reference sheets document Japanese diplomatic requests to permit the Shiriya, Hayatomo, Iro, and Kyokuto Maru to call at Honolulu, Hilo, Los Angeles, and San Francisco to load crude petroleum.
